purpose: Original teaching checks for computational MS generalization, metrics, format scope, and provenance
status: Synthetic arithmetic and logic fixtures; not experimental data, a validated error-control method, or an empirical software benchmark

assumptions: Every peptide has the stated repeated spectra
Both portions include every peptide
Only exact peptide-sequence novelty is assessed
All spectra of a held-out sequence remain outside training
No duplicate underlying sequence or pretraining overlap
No inference about structural-family or instrument novelty
Coordinates already aligned
No omitted peaks
Positive intensity scaling
Synthetic vectors do not establish molecular identity
Truth labels known by construction
This bin is descriptive and retains sampling uncertainty
No implication that ranking is poor
One known correct answer per constructed identification case
At most one reported candidate per case
Incorrect calls do not count as recovered correct identities
Known labels are synthetic
False-call counts are not decoy counts
Illustrated expression is (D+1)/max(T,1)
An appropriate equal-opportunity competition and reporting unit would be required for inferential use
Fixture checks arithmetic only; no FDR guarantee
Threshold-selection procedure is not simulated
Paired nonconstant arrays
No calibration or model fitting implied
First record is explicitly minutes
Second record is explicitly seconds
Equal numeric strings do not imply equal quantities
All three labeled samples occur in each of two fractions
One acquisition file per fraction
Sample-to-file relationship count is not biological replication

roles.mzML: spectra and chromatograms with acquisition/processing metadata
roles.mzTab: identification/quantification results with metadata and evidence links

assumptions: Roles describe primary scope, not every optional extension
Versions and actual exporter behavior remain relevant
A checksum comparison concerns bytes
Scientific interpretation requires additional context
No other claim is being tested
Distinct scan IDs do not imply distinct sequences
Molecular novelty and instrument novelty are separate design axes
Instrument-transfer adaptation must be disclosed when used
